## The core thesis {.section-title}

::: {.kicker}
RELIABILITY COMES FROM THE SYSTEM AROUND THE MODEL
:::

::: {.big-idea}
Treat multi-agent research like a governed analytical pipeline, not a group chat.
:::

::: {.three-col .top-gap}
::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">Control plane</div>

Python owns workflow state, concurrency, budgets, retries, validation, and release policy.
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Inference plane</div>

The OpenAI Agents SDK gives each role a bounded model loop, tools, typed output, and hosted traces.
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Evidence plane</div>

Source records, claims, artifacts, audit history, and eval results remain inspectable after the run.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}

- `src/housing_policy_agents/workflows/research_workflow.py`
- OpenAI Agents SDK, Agents: https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/agents/

## A familiar modeling metaphor

::: {.two-col .wide-left}
::: {.panel .no-pad}
```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    Q["Policy question"] --> X["Feature construction<br/>research plan"]
    X --> E1["Expert model<br/>government"]
    X --> E2["Expert model<br/>legal"]
    X --> E3["Expert model<br/>academic"]
    E1 --> M["Meta-estimator<br/>manager synthesis"]
    E2 --> M
    E3 --> M
    M --> D["Draft report"]
    D --> V["Diagnostics +<br/>constrained re-work"]
    V --> O["Released output<br/>plus audit trail"]
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.callout-blue}
<div class="panel-title">Mixture of experts</div>

Branches specialize by evidence domain. Managers reconcile authority, disagreement, and uncertainty.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">No silent imputation</div>

A failed branch becomes explicit missingness with a typed status and limitation. It does not disappear.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Diagnostics before release</div>

Validation and adversarial review inspect the report after generation, when defects can be localized.
:::
:::
:::

## Who controls what?

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">Python workflow</div>

- Selects branches and managers
- Starts concurrent tasks
- Enforces retries and time limits
- Carries run state and source IDs
- Applies deterministic validators
- Decides whether content is released or withheld
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Agents SDK runtime</div>

- Executes the agent turn loop
- Calls hosted and local tools
- Validates structured model output
- Returns raw responses and usage
- Emits hosted trace spans and metadata
- Supports agents exposed as tools
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
The app keeps policy and reliability decisions in ordinary code. The SDK handles bounded agent execution.
:::

## A bounded SDK call, with tools and trace metadata

::: {.two-col .code-slide}
::: {.panel}
```python
agent = build_specialist_agent(
    branch=assignment.branch.value,
    config=context.config,
    tools=backend.agent_tools(),
)

result = await Runner.run(
    agent,
    input=payload,
    max_turns=config.max_turns_per_agent,
    run_config=RunConfig(
        workflow_name="housing-policy-research",
        trace_id=context.trace_id,
        trace_metadata={
            "run_id": context.run_id,
            "branch": assignment.branch.value,
        },
    ),
)
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>1</b><span>Build the role from versioned instructions and a Pydantic output type.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>2</b><span>Attach the hosted <code>WebSearchTool</code> only in live mode.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>3</b><span>Bound the run with <code>max_turns</code> and workflow policy.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>4</b><span>Group SDK spans with app run and branch metadata.</span>
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}

## Concurrency without losing failure semantics

::: {.two-col .wide-left}
::: {.panel .no-pad}
```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Workflow
    participant S as Semaphore
    participant A as Specialist A
    participant B as Specialist B
    participant C as Specialist C
    W->>S: gather assignments
    S->>A: acquire slot
    S->>B: acquire slot
    S->>C: wait
    A-->>W: COMPLETED finding
    B--xW: parse or tool failure
    W->>B: bounded retry
    B-->>W: FAILED finding + limitation
    S->>C: acquire released slot
    C-->>W: COMPLETED finding
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.callout-blue}
<div class="panel-title">Bounded parallelism</div>

An `asyncio.Semaphore` controls API pressure. `asyncio.gather` preserves branch-level results.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Failure as data</div>

Exceptions are converted to typed failed findings after retries. Managers see the missing branch and its reason.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Partial, never fabricated</div>

If no usable evidence reaches a manager, the fallback is partial coverage, not invented synthesis.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `src/housing_policy_agents/workflows/research_workflow.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/agents/specialists.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/agents/managers.py`
:::

## The source ledger is chain of custody

::: {.four-grid}
::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">01 | Acquire</div>

Specialists retrieve official, legal, academic, industry, advocacy, or comparative evidence.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">02 | Normalize</div>

Every source becomes a `SourceRecord` with a short stable ID, URL, publisher, date, and source tier.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">03 | Join</div>

Claims refer to source IDs. URLs stay in the source record, which keeps citations resolvable and deduplicated.
:::

::: {.panel .mini .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">04 | Validate</div>

The workflow rejects missing references, malformed comparisons, and unsupported report claims.
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
Think of the ledger as data lineage for qualitative evidence: every released claim must have a reproducible path back to a source record.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `src/housing_policy_agents/tools/source_store.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/models/domain.py`
- `docs/architecture.md`
:::

## Validation and re-work are residual diagnostics

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel .no-pad}
```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    D["Draft report"] --> V["Deterministic validation"]
    V --> R["Withhold + re-work<br/>flagged targets"]
    R --> C{"Defect cleared?"}
    C -- "yes" --> P["Replace target"]
    C -- "no" --> W["Keep withheld"]
    P --> A["Audit report"]
    W --> A
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.callout-blue}
<div class="panel-title">Constrained repair</div>

The re-work agent can change only flagged targets. It cannot silently rewrite healthy sections.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Auditable diff</div>

The audit records what failed, what was withheld, the attempted revision, and the final disposition.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Fail closed by section</div>

Unresolved unsupported content remains withheld while valid report sections can still be released.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `src/housing_policy_agents/agents/rework.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/prompts/rework.md`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/tools/source_store.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/workflows/research_workflow.py`
:::

## Adversarial review is the challenger model

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">Primary model</div>

The writer synthesizes manager outputs into a decision-oriented report with claims, caveats, alternatives, and source references.
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Challenger model</div>

The reviewer looks for overclaiming, omitted counterevidence, authority mismatches, weak country analogies, and unsupported recommendations.
:::
:::

::: {.flow-row}
<span>Draft</span><i></i><span>Review findings</span><i></i><span>One bounded revision</span><i></i><span>Final validation</span>
:::

::: {.principle}
Separation of roles matters: generation optimizes coherence; challenge optimizes defect discovery.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `src/housing_policy_agents/agents/writer.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/agents/reviewer.py`
- `src/housing_policy_agents/prompts/writer.md`

:::

## Usage telemetry turns cost into a model diagnostic

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">What is measured</div>

- Requests per interaction
- Input, cached input, output, and reasoning tokens
- Wall-clock duration per agent and stage
- Completed or failed status
- Model and pricing version
:::

::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">What is estimated</div>

<div class="cost-formula">C<sub>est</sub> = (t<sub>in</sub>r<sub>in</sub> + t<sub>cache</sub>r<sub>cache</sub> + t<sub>out</sub>r<sub>out</sub>) / 10<sup>6</sup></div>

The estimate is useful for branch and architecture comparisons. It is explicitly labeled as an estimate, not an invoice.
:::
:::

::: {.warning-strip}
Hosted tool charges, service-tier adjustments, taxes, credits, and later pricing changes are outside this estimate.
:::

::: {.notes}

## A Python provider makes the whole workflow testable

::: {.two-col .code-slide}
::: {.panel}
```python
def call_api(prompt, options, context):
    config = AppConfig(
        research_provider="offline",
        enable_manager_reconciliation=True,
        enable_adversarial_review=True,
    )
    request = UserResearchRequest(
        question=context["vars"]["question"],
        mode=RunMode.FAST,
        accept_defaults=True,
    )
    package = asyncio.run(
        ResearchWorkflow(config).run(request)
    )
    return {
        "output": package.model_dump_json(),
        "metadata": {"run_id": package.run_id},
    }
```
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>1</b><span>Promptfoo calls a normal Python function.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>2</b><span>The provider constructs the same application workflow used by the CLI.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>3</b><span>The structured package becomes assertion input.</span>
:::
::: {.numbered-step}
<b>4</b><span>Run metadata links a failed eval back to artifacts and traces.</span>
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]
- `evals/providers/hierarchical_provider.py`
- Promptfoo Python provider: https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/providers/python/

## Compare architectures, then ablate mechanisms

::: {.two-col .wide-left}
::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Baseline comparison</div>

| Variant | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Full hierarchy | Candidate production architecture |
| Shallow baseline | Tests whether complexity earns its cost |

<div class="panel-title">Factorial ablations</div>

| Removed mechanism | Question answered |
|---|---|
| Legal branch | Does legal evidence improve validity? |
| Manager reconciliation | Does aggregation reduce contradictions? |
| Adversarial review | Does challenge improve defect recall? |
| Clarification | Does better intake improve downstream quality? |
:::

::: {.stack}
::: {.callout-blue}
<div class="panel-title">Offline first</div>

Fixture-backed runs are deterministic and cheap. They test orchestration, schemas, assertions, and artifact production.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Live second</div>

Live evals add retrieval and model variance. Use them selectively for realism after the harness is stable.
:::

::: {.callout-gray}
<div class="panel-title">Evaluate trajectories too</div>

SDK spans can be bridged to OTLP so Promptfoo can assert tool and agent trajectories, not only final text.
:::
:::
:::

## Assertions turn architecture goals into observables

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">Structural correctness</div>

- Output schema validates
- Required report sections exist
- Source IDs resolve
- Citation fabrication stays below threshold
- Seeded defects are recalled
:::

::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">Research behavior</div>

- Prompt injection is resisted
- Primary sources are represented
- Source diversity clears the floor
- Unnecessary agent activation stays bounded
- Review and audit artifacts are present
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
Good assertions inspect the structured product and its provenance. A fluent final paragraph is a weak test oracle.
:::

## A practical build sequence

::: {.four-grid}
::: {.panel .mini .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">1 | Contract first</div>

Define typed inputs, outputs, statuses, IDs, and failure representations before writing prompts.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">2 | Control plane</div>

Implement workflow state, concurrency, retries, event recording, and deterministic release rules in code.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">3 | Bounded agents</div>

Give each role a narrow objective, tools, source hierarchy, scope exclusions, and structured output type.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">4 | Trace every edge</div>

Persist handoffs, results, durations, usage, source lineage, validation findings, and report revisions.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">5 | Deterministic harness</div>

Create offline fixtures and assertions for the workflow before spending tokens on live evaluation.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">6 | Comparative evals</div>

Test a shallow baseline, full system, and mechanism ablations against the same dataset.
:::

::: {.panel .mini}
<div class="panel-title">7 | Failure drills</div>

Inject parse failures, missing branches, bad citations, prompt attacks, and re-work failures.
:::

::: {.panel .mini .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">8 | Release policy</div>

Decide what is revised, withheld, or released, then make that decision auditable.
:::
:::

## Production judgment: where to be skeptical

::: {.two-col}
::: {.panel}
<div class="panel-title">This architecture improves</div>

- Separation of research responsibilities
- Failure localization
- Citation and source traceability
- Reproducible evaluation
- Cost and latency attribution
- Selective withholding instead of all-or-nothing failure
:::

::: {.panel .accent-top}
<div class="panel-title">It does not eliminate</div>

- Retrieval gaps and stale sources
- Model interpretation errors
- Correlated errors across agents
- Prompt and schema regressions
- Evaluation blind spots
- Need for human judgment on consequential policy conclusions
:::
:::

::: {.principle}
Multi-agent structure is useful only when it makes evidence, decisions, failures, and costs more legible.
:::
